description: Team Umai is a two-person team from Kazakhstan. Steppe fires burn across our country every year, and in June 2023 the Abai fire killed 14 forestry workers. So we built ClearCount: one honest burning calendar for Kazakhstan, from 2000 to today.
summary:
In June 2023 the Abai fire killed 14 forestry workers in Kazakhstan. Was that month exceptional? Raw satellite data cannot say: when VIIRS joined MODIS in 2012, Kazakhstan's hotspot counts jumped ×4.6 while nothing changed on the ground, and on 2 November 2026 Suomi NPP went dark. ClearCount answers in one click: June 2023 around Semey burned 32 times a normal June, more than any June of 2003–2021.

ClearCount is a live web app, rebuilt every night, that turns 4.16 million NASA FIRMS hotspots from five satellites (2000 to today) into one consistent burning calendar for Kazakhstan. It calibrates every sensor to MODIS Aqua by region, season and day/night, removes gas flares (17% of detections), carries the record onto NOAA-20, and marks the months when a zero meant "clouds", not "no fire".

Tested on years the calibration never saw, it matches real MODIS counts within ±1% a year (±7% for Abai), and every area a user draws gets its own reliability score. The payoff: raw data says fire is rising in 12 of Kazakhstan's 14 regions; on ClearCount it is falling in all 14.
details:
1. THE PROBLEM

  • Raw counts lie across time. When VIIRS joined MODIS in 2012, Kazakhstan's hotspot counts jumped ×4.6 although nothing changed on the ground (Pettitt test p < 0.001).
  • The record is breaking. Suomi NPP stopped on 2 November 2026 and MODIS is retiring, so 26 years of history can no longer be compared with today.
  • A zero is ambiguous. It can mean "no fire" or "the satellites could not see" because of cloud.

2. WHAT CLEARCOUNT DOES

  • A live web app, rebuilt every night from NASA data, that answers one question for any area of Kazakhstan: is this month unusual compared with every year since 2000?
  • 4,160,745 NASA FIRMS hotspots from 5 satellites (MODIS Terra and Aqua; VIIRS Suomi NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21), November 2000 to today.
  • Draw an area, type coordinates or pick a region to get the month against its 2003–2021 median with a 95% interval, a burning calendar with cloud-blind months hatched, season-to-date, trends, an early-warning model and a reliability score for that exact area.
  • Downloads: CSV, PNG, PDF and the full harmonized record as open data. English, Russian and Kazakh. A 2-minute guided tour for first-time users.

3. HOW IT WORKS

  • Clean. A multi-year persistence mask removes gas flares and industrial heat: 17% of all detections.
  • Calibrate. MODIS Aqua is the reference. Every VIIRS detection gets a weight from a shrunken ratio estimator (national → 3° block → season, day and night separately). Terra bridges 2000–2002.
  • Continue. NOAA-20 takes over from Suomi NPP through a validated hand-over.
  • Explain. Real swath footprints from NASA CMR show why VIIRS sees 5.3× more fire: 1.3× more passes, each 4.1× more sensitive.
  • Blind or quiet. Daily cloud cover (NASA POWER / CERES) and per-pass Level-2 MODIS fire masks separate "no fire" from "could not see". A Poisson gradient-boosting model estimates the fires hidden by cloud (≈22% in the fire season), tested by artificially blinding clear days.

4. PROOF: SIX TESTS ON DATA THE METHOD NEVER SAW

  • Held-out years 2018–2021: yearly totals within ±1% nationally (±7% for the Abai area), R² = 0.92 on log monthly counts, bias −1.8%.
  • The 2012 break disappears: Pettitt p < 0.001 on raw data, p = 0.74 on ClearCount.
  • Independent NASA burned area (MCD64A1): raw hotspots per km² burned rose ×8.2 after 2012; ClearCount only +14%.
  • Transfer to Mongolia, never used in fitting: bias 8%, versus 37% for a naive ratio.
  • Losing Suomi NPP, simulated on 2024–2025: NOAA-20 chain / S-NPP chain = 1.001, monthly Spearman ρ = 0.993.
  • Orbit-drift detector: Aqua +17.6%, Terra −33.8%, with a NOAA-20 placebo within ±5%.

5. CASE: THE ABAI FIRE, JUNE 2023

  • June 2023 in the Abai fire area was 32× the median June, above every June of 2003–2021.
  • On 10 June the hotspots dropped to zero (39 on 9 June, 56 on 11 June). ClearCount checked every satellite pass: the daytime passes were 69–100% cloud, so the satellites were blind; the night passes were clear and saw no fire, because it had quietened under 2.9 mm of rain.
  • A raw count reads 10 June as "no fire". ClearCount shows what happened and why.

6. WHAT THE HONEST RECORD REVEALS

  • The trend flips. Raw FIRMS says Kazakhstan's fires are rising 5.6% a year; the harmonized record shows them falling 8.5% a year (Mann–Kendall p < 0.001), consistent with published studies of the Kazakh steppe.
  • Region by region. Raw data shows fire rising in 12 of 14 regions (significantly in 8). On ClearCount it is falling in all 14 (significantly in 13).
  • Better forecasts. The same early-warning model scores AUC 0.72 on harmonized history versus 0.68 on raw history.

7. WHO IT HELPS

  • Emergency managers: a trustworthy "is this unusual?" for any area, refreshed every night.
  • Land managers: when cropland burning peaks (April–May) and where.
  • Scientists: trends that are not sensor artifacts, ready for the post-MODIS era, with open data.
  • Beyond Kazakhstan: the Mongolia test shows the calibration transfers to other countries.

8. TECH STACK

  • Pipeline: Python (pandas, NumPy, SciPy, scikit-learn, earthaccess, h5py, pyhdf).
  • Web app: JavaScript (Leaflet, Leaflet.draw, d3.js).
  • Hosting: GitHub Actions and GitHub Pages, no paid services. Open source: https://github.com/dede-bebe-lele/clearcount

9. TEAM UMAI

  • Dariya Nuralina: team captain and lead developer.
  • Yasin Zhalgasbaeva: testing and localization.
